column1: # Rule triage: which standing rules can be machine-enforced, and which genuinely cannot.
# Verdict is JUDGMENT only. A rule that can be gated does not belong here; it belongs in
# a hook or a check, and the rule bullet names it. Absence from this file plus absence of
# a named gate is the decay surface, reported by scripts/find-decayed-rules.py.
# JUDGMENT is not an excuse. It means: a detector would fire on the wrong things, and a
# check that cries wolf gets disabled, which is worse than no check. Each row says why.
# The key is what find-decayed-rules.py derives from the bullet's first bolded phrase;
# run it with --untriaged to see the exact key for a new rule.

column3: Governs whether to ask before acting. The signal is the conversation, not any file. No artifact to inspect.
Governs what the agent does after a write. The substance is whether the destination was queried, which leaves no trace in the repo.
Whether a promise was exercised end to end. A passing test proves the test ran, never that the right thing was tested.
A routing choice made in conversation. The guard blocks the wrong write; whether the agent then drives the right lane or hands back the window is not visible to a check.
Two sessions in one checkout leave no file-level signature until they collide. A per-lane lockfile would gate it; until one exists this is judgment, and the doc says so.
Whether a session asked a neighbour before re-deriving work is a conversation event, not a repo state.
Replies are not files. No check can see them. Enforced by being specific enough that a missing HEADLINE is visible to the reader.
A reply-shape rule. The reply-length pair measures length and self-narration; the substance of a corrected fact is not detectable.
Whether a queued request was resumed is conversation state with no artifact.
A clock written into a file has a signature; a clock spoken in chat does not. The chat half is the one that decays, and it is model-side.
Depends on who the reader is. No detector can know that.
Negotiation posture in copy the human sends. Too varied in wording for a pattern that does not also match legitimate offers.
A handoff is a prompt, not a file. Its shape is visible to the reader, not to a check.
Non-trivial is a judgment. A hook that fires on every new file is noise; /preflight is the mechanism and skipping it is the miss.
Whether a judgment call was logged or silently absorbed cannot be detected from the code. /ship reads the log; an empty one is not evidence of none.
Whether a change went through the ship flow is not recoverable from the commit. The commit gate covers the mechanical half.
Whether the corpus was actually read before drafting is a conversation event. The linter catches a draft that reads wrong, never a session that skipped the samples and got lucky.
Which samples a draft was built from leaves no trace in the draft. The directory split makes the wrong pull inconvenient; choosing the right one stays judgment.
A rule about how the next check is introduced. A check that gated this one would have to judge whether a check was ready, which is the judgment being made.
